title: Development charges rules and U.S. tariff response
subtitle: Tariff task force update, a demolition approval on Clive Road, and recognition of racial discrimination and COVID anniversaries
overview: Council directed staff to interpret the provincial development charges discount and deferral for rental housing as not applying to condominium developments or street-fronting townhouse developments {{vote:m1}}. The direction follows legal advice in a staff report and leaves the application to the City Treasurer and City Solicitor. This affects what charges those builders pay.

Staff updated Council on the City's Tariff and Trade Task Force, formed after a February resolution. Proposed actions include amending the procurement by-law to favour Canadian and local purchasing, talking with city vendors about Canadian alternatives, supporting local businesses, and a Support Local campaign with business improvement areas, the Chamber of Commerce and the Kitchener Market. No decision was taken on this item. A report with recommendations is expected at the April 1 Council meeting.

Council also approved the demolition of a two-storey single detached home at 101 Clive Road {{vote:m3}}. The Mayor marked the International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination and the five-year anniversary of the COVID-19 pandemic, with a moment of silence. Council then met in closed session on a labour relations or employee negotiation matter.

decisions.detail: Staff were directed to treat the rental housing development discount and deferral as not applying to condominium and street-fronting townhouse developments, at the discretion of the City Treasurer and City Solicitor.
Council approved demolition control application DC25/002/C/AS to demolish a two-storey single detached dwelling at 101 Clive Road.

debate: Councillors asked how the City will hear from and keep informing local businesses. Staff said they are meeting tariff-exposed companies one-on-one, will convene small businesses through the Small Business Centre, and have set up a web page and e-news updates.

On local manufacturing, staff said the quickest help is connecting companies that now buy from the U.S. with Canadian suppliers, working with the regional economic development corporation, and passing on federal and provincial support programs.

One councillor suggested sharing a list of local suppliers with other Ontario municipalities that buy the same goods and services. Staff called the idea worth exploring and said regional work on import substitution is a first step.

Another councillor asked that the City reach out to local unions and the regional labour council, since their members could be affected. Staff agreed to bring this to the task force as stakeholder outreach widens.
Councillors thanked staff for the quick work. One urged thoughtful, lasting engagement with businesses and residents.
